newsitem.title: NORWAY: Elkem expects unchanged demand in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Elkem expects unchanged demand in 1997.

text.p: Norwegian metals maker Elkem ASA said on Tuesday it expected demand for its products to stay at about the same level this year as in 1996.

"At the end of the first quarter, there was some increase in the supply of ferroalloys, and this put pressure on prices. This situation is likely to continue," Elkem said in a statement accompanying the release of the 1996 profits.
"Aluminium prices have increased at the beginning of the first quarter, and relatively stable prices are expected in the short term," it said.
It said silicon metal market prices were also expected to stabilise in the short term.

"A large part of Elkem's production has already been sold on annual contracts that are higher than those achieved in 1996, and the Group's income in this area is less exposed to market developments," it said.

"The appreciation of the Norwegian crown will have a negative impact on Elkem's result. Seen in isolation, every percent that the NOK appreciates has a negative effect on Elkem of about NOK 30 million.
"The effect of the strengthening of the NOK will be less in 1997, since the company has hedged about three quarters of its expected income," it said.
Elkem also said it was currently negotiating with Icelandic authorities about increasing its interest in the ferrosilicon company Icelandic Alloys.
